texts: Pulmonary overcirculation is the least likely complication here: D.
A 4.0-mm shunt is the usual size for a 4-kg baby, and with the duct ligated and pulmonary atresia it is the only source of lung blood flow, so flooding is unlikely.

A shunt through a sternotomy, from the innominate or right subclavian artery to the right PA, can injure the right recurrent laryngeal nerve, distort or narrow the right PA where it is sewn, and thrombose.
PTFE grafts can also weep serous fluid and form a seroma round the shunt.
In the picture, the money sacks drink calmly while the rein is nicked, the pipe pinched, the beaver builds his dam and the clear blister swells.
Memory hook: four for four: the sacks drink calmly.
